assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. It combines a very large instrumented-ice detector with clear physics outcomes, including the diffuse flux, the 2017 TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane observation. From an experimental astroparticle perspective this is a decisive instrument-plus-discovery case with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver of the concept and the collaboration's long-term leader. Karle and Spiering are credited as senior contributors to construction and the discovery analyses. A collaboration of hundreds makes any three-person split somewhat arbitrary, and I cannot independently verify the relative weights of individual roles.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed repeatedly with multiple event topologies and analysis methods. The source identification is still partial, but the discovery itself is stable and timely.
uncertainties: Relative weighting of Halzen, Karle, Spiering and other collaboration leaders is uncertain.
Source populations remain only partly identified, so the astrophysical interpretation is incomplete.
Whether the committee would prefer to wait for stronger source associations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon strip and pixel detectors made precision vertexing and tracking routine at colliders and underpin heavy-flavour physics, the Higgs discoveries and many space-based instruments. The technique is an enabling invention with huge and demonstrable downstream impact, in line with the Prize's recognition of instrumentation.
assessment.attribution: Parker (microstrip detectors), Weilhammer and colleagues (planar silicon strips, NA11/NA32 and later) and Heijne (pixel and hybrid concepts) each have recognisable roles. Credit is shared with others such as Kemmer (planar process) who are not in the supplied names, so the fair allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been in sustained use for about four decades with broad independent adoption, so it is very mature. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Kemmer and other planar-process and CCD-related contributors are not among the supplied names.
Priority between strip and pixel lines is blurred and I cannot verify specific dates from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model's particle content and rests on extraordinary detector and analysis work. The theoretical prediction was recognised in 2013, but the experimental discovery has not been, and its scientific importance is beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the central problem. Thousands of people contributed, and the supplied names are collaboration spokespersons and detector pioneers rather than analysis discoverers. I selected the proposers of the CMS and ATLAS detector concepts and the discovery-era spokesperson, but Jenni's equal claim and the claim of many others cannot be resolved here. The prize rules on number of laureates make this difficult.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been confirmed with detailed measurements of couplings, so the science is mature and the recognition is overdue in timing, though the attribution puzzle may keep delaying it.
uncertainties: No fair three-person configuration exists for a collaboration discovery of this scale.
Excluding Peter Jenni is hard to justify scientifically.
Whether an organisational prize is feasible under the statutes is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the field of moire quantum matter and twistronics. It is a new, highly original platform with rapid conceptual impact across condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction of the magic angle and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery. This is a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other groups, including those with early STM and transport work, have claims that are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have replicated and extended the results, although the nature of the superconductivity is still debated. The field is active, and some may view recognition as slightly early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled.
Other experimental groups and Kim-style hBN-enabled work may deserve credit but are not among the names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock concept and its realisation with magic-wavelength trapping gave clocks with 1e-18 fractional uncertainty, and opened new tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. A precise measurement advance with clear lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye's group delivered the best realisations. Both are central, and the pair is a natural configuration, though Hall and Hansen already received the 2005 prize for the frequency comb that enabled these clocks.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have confirmed the performance, and redefinition of the second is being discussed. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Contributions from other lattice clock groups, such as Lemonde, Ludlow and Bloom, are not credited.
Overlap with the earlier frequency comb prize may affect the committee's view of originality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ground-based imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes established very-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy and revealed many source classes, including supernova remnants and pulsar wind nebulae. This is a field I know well as an experimentalist, and the instrumentation path from Whipple through HEGRA to H.E.S.S. is a scientific story with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Hofmann led HEGRA and H.E.S.S. instrumentation and Aharonian led the scientific programme, including the HEGRA results. Weekes (Whipple, Crab detection) is a major omission from the supplied names, and the credit without him is unfair.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature with CTA/CTAO on the horizon and well confirmed across many facilities. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Trevor Weekes, who is not in the supplied credit, has a prior claim.
Credit between the instrument builders and the astrophysical interpretation is hard to apportion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal and realisation of controlled quantum information processing with trapped ions and neutral atoms is conceptually fundamental and connected to quantum computing and quantum simulation. The Cirac-Zoller gate and its experimental demonstration are landmark results.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion gate and many theory ideas, and Blatt led major experimental realisations. Bloch is excluded in this configuration, though his claim is better seated in the lattice simulation candidate. Wineland's 2012 prize overlaps with this area.
assessment.maturity: Experimental progress is strong and independently replicated across many groups. Recognition is plausible but the practical applications are still developing, so maturity is partial.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 and 2022 prizes in quantum optics and information.
Choice between ions and atoms and between Blatt and Bloch is a difficult allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, created a major subfield of condensed matter physics. Its importance and originality are high, though it builds on the 2016 topology prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction, and Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation, following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's prediction. The omission of Zhang, who is deceased, and others complicates the credit chain.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed across materials platforms, including 3D topological insulators. The science is mature, although the recognition may be seen as partly covered by 2016.
uncertainties: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not credited here, and Zhang's death affects eligibility.
Overlap with the 2016 Nobel topological-phase prize.
